column1: # Each row: FILE <TAB> SNIPPET-KEY (whitespace-stripped) <TAB> STATUS <TAB> REASON
# STATUS = SAFE (judged a non-bug) | BUG (open, needs a real byte measure).
# A byte-cap comparison NOT listed here reads as NEW and fails `--check`.
# THE QUESTION for each site: can the string whose `.length` is compared to the
#   • base64 / hex / ASCII-only  → .length == byte count → SAFE
#   • JSON blob / user text / transcript / prompt → must use Buffer.byteLength,
#     TextEncoder().encode(s).length, new Blob([s]).size, or (localStorage) *2 → else BUG
# All current sites measure a base64 data-URL string (`dataBase64`), which is pure
# ASCII, so char count EQUALS byte count. Several carry a `* 1.4` slack factor for
# the base64→binary expansion ratio — that is the correct budget for the inline-image
# wire cost, not a UTF-16 mistake. The historical BUGS in this class (Westchester
# state-sync, Nile-flights, snapshot vault, commentbank corpus) measured JSON/text
# blobs and have all been migrated to real byte measures, so they no longer appear
